speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) how will the UN High Seas Treaty affect Singapore's plans on maritime conservation; and (b) how will it impact Singapore's plans to build polders or other mitigation against rising sea levels as well as the Greater Southern Waterfront Gateway development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The treaty governs areas in the high seas and deep seabed – in other words, the waters and the seabed beyond the 200 nautical mile exclusive economic zone and continental shelves of countries, and is beyond the jurisdiction of any country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Through the treaty, our scientists and researchers will share information and marine samples with other parties, and the scientists and researchers of other parties will do likewise with us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This can help to contribute to global conservation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The more we understand about marine biodiversity in the high seas and deep seabed, the better we will be able to protect it.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Singapore is one of the busiest maritime ports in the world.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Will the BBNJ Agreement have any effect on our sea lines of communications?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I also ask whether the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) is equally supportive on the global treaty to end plastic pollution, and how is Singapore contributing to that as well?
